items.title: Mike De Lay Interview, 1970-11-14
items.q: when you talk about real players, who my favorites was like Buddy Petit, Kid Punch, you know what I mean, Kid Punch? Well, I used to love him when I was a kid. Now, he was one of my real favorites.

ctx.x: Mike, when you were playing up, do you consider the best cornet player?

Oh, that's a kind of hard thing. Sure. To say, because you know the reason why, when I was a kid, you're talking about it? Yeah. Because I was listening to the cornet and trumpets all my, what's that cornet then, that damn night. All my days, I just loved it. My mother wouldn't buy me one. She wouldn't buy me a violin. I didn't want to buy me. But anyway, I had my, well, before Ludd, John Tron came along, I was crazy about my teacher, Manuel Perez. He had such a name around there, you know, around him. He, when…
I said, plenty gold on the lawn socks. No, I didn't know.

items.title: Mike De Lay Interview, 1958-09-02
items.q: So I just, I had an idea, I always wanted to play on that type, just a lot of execution.

ctx.x: Well in the parades, well I remember, well I know, I tell you one thing, the favorite one, one of the main favorites of the kids was Lewis Armstrong. Because all they had to say, oh yes, here come Lewis Armstrong and all the kids just tear out the house. Oh yes, everybody used to tear, you know, you know second line of the halls, I know you know about that. Oh yeah, I remember that. And gosh, and they were loaded I think. But I mean, the music always did touch me, no kidding, I mean, I just like it and always,…
Can you tell more about his style? Because John said Buddy Pt, that you play like him sometimes, you play a little chorus and

all that. Buddy Pt, well, what I would say was a lot of, in those days they used to call it runs, we call them chords nowadays, you know, breaking chords, you know what I mean? Because you get to, in later years we studied those things and we actually properly, in other words, probably naturally knew what we were doing. You would put it that way, you understand what I mean? So I just, I had an idea, I always wanted to play on that type, just a lot of execution. And even before, even before I knew, I knew too…
